capitals.note: The infobox lists Srinagar for 1320-1323, 1339-1343, 1354-1470, 1472-1529 and 1530-1586, Sikandarpur for 1470-1472 and Naushahra for 1529-1530, then Chandrakot 1586-1587, Varmul 1587-1588, Suyyapur 1586-1588 and 'no centralised capital' 1588-1589. 1531: Kamran Mirza's Mughal army takes Srinagar. 'Mughal forces under Kamran Mirza sacked Srinagar in 1531 and were routed by Kaji Chak'; the Chak page: the army 'conquered almost all forts and cities, including Srinagar, except Athwajan'.
1531: the Mughals are routed by Kaji Chak; the page gives no other year for the end.

region.text: the Kashmir Valley, held by Mirza Haidar for Humayun

ledger.note: December 1540: Haidar Dughlat, serving Humayun, attacks in November 1540 and Kashmir 'was formally annexed in December 1540'; infobox 'Mughal Interregnum: December 1540 - October 1551'. The Chak page has Dughlat as Mughal governor installing Nazuk Shah as sultan, so the sultanate's line survives under occupation.
October 1551: the Mughal Interregnum ends (infobox 'December 1540 - October 1551'). The Chak page names no end year.

1561: the Chaks replace the Shah Miris within the same sultanate. The Chak page: the dynasty 'rose to power in 1561 in Srinagar' when Ghazi Shah deposed Habib Shah, 'the last Shah Miri sultan'; the Kashmir Sultanate page: Habib Shah (1557-1561), 'dethroned ... in 1561'.

December 1585: the Mughal invasion begins. Infobox '20 December 1585 - 8 August 1589'; 'on 31 December 1585, an army led by Mirza Shah Rukh and Raja Bhagwant Das' set out; Yusuf Shah Chak submitted on 24 February 1586, and Akbar rejected the treaty and imprisoned him.

ledger.counterpart: page silent: the Maqpon Kingdom, which supported the Mughals
ledger.note: Baltistan stands with the Mughals: the infobox lists 'Mughal Empire (supported by Maqpon Kingdom)'. The page does not say how or when the Maqpons left the sultanate's orbit, so the year is the war's start.

October 1586: the Mughals win the Battle of Hastivanj on 10 October 1586 and take Srinagar on 14 October 1586 (Kashmir Sultanate infobox; the Mughal page has only the battle date). The Mughal infobox and the Chak page carry the war and the dynasty to 8 August 1589.

14 October 1586: the Mughals hold Srinagar. 'Fall of Srinagar: 14 October 1586'; 'Mughal rule was formally instigated on 14 October 1586'; the Chak page: Yakub Shah 'dethroned on 14 October 1586 by the Mughals', who 'kept using the title of Sultan of Kashmir until 1589'. The Mughal infobox calls the result 'Annexation of Kashmir Valley'; the occupation is drawn until the surrender so that the hand-over falls in 1589 with the mughal-empire dossier.

8 August 1589: the occupation ends in the annexation of the Valley (Chak page: 'dissolution: 8 August 1589', Yakub Shah surrendered to Akbar; Mughal infobox: war ends 8 August 1589). The Akbar page in the mughal-empire dossier has the surrender received at Srinagar in June 1589.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary. The Valley is the least uncertain; the hills, Ladakh, Baltistan, Gilgit, Pakhli and Swat are approximate, and every year of the conquests and of Baltistan's departure is a bracket.

notes: Kashmiri Sultanate: twelve Cliopatria shapes (1344-1587) reviewed against five pages (Kashmir Sultanate, Zayn al-Abidin, Shihabu'd-Din Shah, Chak dynasty, Mughal conquest of Kashmir), the budget. Findings: Cliopatria's 1344 outline carries Xinjiang (90 cells), Xizang (21), Ladakh (224) and Baltistan (65), none of which any page puts in the sultanate before Shihabu'd-Din; its 1352-1587 outlines are the Valley, the hills and 220 Ladakh cells, with only 5 Baltistan and 18 Pakhli cells and no Gilgit or Swat, which the pages name. The corrections are two shapes, a smaller one before the conquests (310 cells, about 87,000 km2, 1339-1369) and a larger one after (834 cells, about 232,000 km2, 1370-1584), each in Cliopatria's own words plus the named lands. Infobox areas: 222,236 km2 (1342) and 250,000 km2 (1389). The 1389 figure fits the larger shape; the 1342 figure is 2.5 times the smaller one and I did not follow it, because the text puts the greatest extent under Shihabu'd-Din and gives no land for 1342. Dates: start 1339 (Cliopatria 1344; infobox Lohara war 1338-1339). End 8 August 1589 (Chak page and Mughal infobox; Yakub Shah kept the title); Srinagar fell on 14 October 1586 (Kashmir Sultanate infobox, Chak page), drawn as an occupation to 1589 so that the hand-over matches the mughal-empire dossier (gain June 1589); Cliopatria ends the row in 1587. The conquests of Shihabu'd-Din (reign 19 April 1354 - 6 June 1373) have no year on any page; the only anchor is his return to Srinagar 'around 1370', so the gains carry 1370 at confidence 1. Not drawn: the cession of land 'from Sirhind to Kashmir' under the peace with Firuz Shah (the Kashmir Sultanate page says west of the Sutlej; both undated; it would overlay the Tughlaq Punjab), Pothohar, Ohind, Kishtwar, Chamba, Jammu and the hill states (inside the Cliopatria outline from 1344 and so already in both shapes; the page says Malik Candra 'subdued' them under Shihabu'd-Din), the 'lapse' implied by 'Ladakh and Baltistan re-annexed' under Zayn al-Abidin, and the capital moves to Sikandarpur (1470-1472) and Naushahra (1529-1530), not in the gazetteer. Page disagreements: the Kashmir Sultanate page's lead says the Chak rule continued 'to the Mughal conquest in 1586' and their surrender in 1589; its caption 'Kashmir Sultanate in 1525' is unexplained, and the Shah Mir entry in the infobox runs from 1339 while the Lohara interruption also runs to 1339; the Mughal page gives 14 October only for 1592. Hand-offs: the mughal-empire dossier (sa-05) already has contest_start 1585 and a gain of Kashmir in June 1589 (Akbar page); this dossier agrees on 1589 and adds the Mughal occupation of the Valley from 14 October 1586, which that dossier does not draw (its contest runs to 1589); Cliopatria draws Kashmir as Mughal from 1588. The Maqpon Kingdom (Baltistan), the Maryuls of Ladakh and the Kishtwar Kingdom would need dossiers if wanted. Region names: Pakhli, Swat, Sikandarpur, Naushahra, Kishtwar, Chamba, Pothohar, Ohind are missing from the gazetteer; Pakhli and Swat are drawn as 70 km circles.
